D5·23b6 — 2026-09-15
rule: A Rust perf claim is made only with `npm run perf` numbers (SOFAR_CONFORMANCE_BIN, same machine as a fresh reference run), never with in-process or hand-timed figures; the 3.3 gate is every cell's p50 and p95 at or under the recorded target.
chose: The perf target for the Rust core is the checked-in TypeScript baseline (packages/engine/test/conformance/perf/baseline.typescript.json), recorded by the 1.3 runner with the same black-box method the conformance suite uses (one process per hook, spawn to exit, p50/p95 nearest rank over 20 spawns) across 10/100/1,000 initiatives × 1/10 MB bound logs, this repo's record and a no-record floor. The 3.3 gate (SOFAR_PERF_GATE=1) passes only when every candidate p50 AND p95 is ≤ the target in every cell, candidate and reference re-measured on the same machine in the same sitting.
over: In-process micro-benchmarks of fold/render (would not count node boot, the part Rust removes, and cannot run against a binary); a single aggregate score (would let a 10 MB regression hide behind a 1 MB win); comparing against numbers recorded on another machine.
because: The user pays per spawn, so the measurement must include process start and be runnable against any implementation binary; per-cell p50 and p95 is the smallest set that catches both a median regression and a tail regression at each scale; hardware differences dwarf the margins being gated.
